title: About
text:
I’m a product person who builds. For two years I designed, launched, and supported my own products end to end: a generative-AI SaaS, a commission-free restaurant marketplace, and privacy-first iOS apps. That meant doing every job in the loop, from customer interviews and pricing to instrumentation, support tickets, and the call to keep going or stop.
The habit I took from it is short loops. Talk to users, ship the smallest thing that tests the real assumption, instrument it properly, then read what actually happened. One product reached 23,000 monthly organic visitors and I still shut it down, because the infrastructure economics never worked at that conversion rate. Another grew to roughly 1,000 daily active users on word of mouth alone, so it got my attention instead.
Before that I spent two and a half years at talabat as an embedded product data scientist, working alongside product managers, engineers, and designers across Authentication & Onboarding, Home Feed, Search, Pickup, and Vendor. I defined product metrics and health KPIs, ran the experiments behind launches in eight markets, and gave go/no-go calls on features reaching millions of daily users. On the Vendor side I partnered on a targeted discounts platform in Egypt and the UAE that scaled past 15,000 daily orders within six months.
So I come to product from the measurement side, and I’ve since run the whole thing myself. I can write the tracking plan, query the warehouse, and build the prototype, which tends to shorten the distance between a question and an answer.
I’m looking for a product manager, product owner, or founding role where shipping and validating quickly matters more than managing a process. Get in touch.

title: On-Device LLM Agent for iOS
text: An LLM agent that runs entirely on the device: no network calls, no server, no data leaving the phone. It handles tool-calling and context management against small open models running locally.

title: On-Device LLM Agent for iOS
text:
Models
Evaluated and tuned Gemma, Qwen3, and Liquid AI’s LFM on-device, comparing them on three axes that matter once you leave the datacenter:

Latency: time to first token and sustained throughput on Apple Silicon
Memory footprint: what actually fits alongside a normal iOS app budget
Reasoning quality: whether tool-calling stays reliable at these sizes

title: On-Device LLM Agent for iOS
text:
Retrieval
The agent recalls personal notes and memories through an offline retrieval-augmented pipeline over an Obsidian vault, using Apple’s on-device Foundation Models for embedding generation and semantic retrieval.
The no-network constraint shaped the design. Embeddings, index, and generation all stay local, which rules out the usual hosted embedding APIs and vector databases.

title: Commission-Free Restaurant Ordering

A commission-free ordering platform built as three applications, one each for customer, merchant, and rider, aimed at restaurants that lose margin to delivery marketplace fees.
Product-market fit was tested the slow way: customer discovery interviews and onboarding local restaurant partners directly, rather than assuming the commission-free pitch would sell itself.

Open to product manager, product owner, and founding roles. hamza-rabi@outlook.com




Discovery & validation
